findings.title: Default/CI mode never enforces the ADOPTED-PATCHED writer additive-only contract
findings.evidence:
# C. ADOPTED-PATCHED diff is frontmatter-only AND additive (needs upstream)
        for r in rows:
            if r.cls != "ADOPTED-PATCHED":
                continue
            if not upstream_has(upstream_dir, r.path):
                errors.append(f"{r.path}: ADOPTED-PATCHED but absent from upstream checkout")
                continue
            up = prefix_rewrite(upstream_blob(upstream_dir, r.path))
            cur = read_text(_safe_repo_path(r.path))
            if body_of(cur) != body_of(up):
                errors.append(f"{r.path}: body changed — adopted agent bodies must be "
                              f"byte-identical")
            added, removed = frontmatter_line_diff(up, cur)
            if removed:
                errors.append(f"{r.path}: frontmatter lines removed — patch must be "
                              f"additive only ({removed})")
            bad = [ln for ln in added if not ln.strip().startswith("- laf-adaptation:")]
            if bad:
                errors.append(f"{r.path}: only additive `- laf-adaptation:<skill>` skill "
                              f"lines are permitted (offending: {bad})")
    else:
        print("NOTE: verify running without --upstream — Rules B and C (upstream-diff "
              "checks) skipped; Rule A hash-match covers adopted-file integrity against the "
              "recorded manifest, plus Rules D/E/F.")
findings.why: The only code that proves `agents/writer.md` is body-identical and frontmatter-additive is Rule C, and Rule C is skipped whenever `verify()` is run without `--upstream`. CI invokes `uv run python scripts/check_boundary.py` without `--upstream`, so a PR can edit the ADOPTED-PATCHED writer body and update only its `laf_sha256` manifest value; Rule A passes, A′ explicitly excludes ADOPTED-PATCHED rows, and Rule C never runs. That leaves the showcased boundary-contract exception unenforced in the PR gate.
findings.recommendation: Either run Mode U in CI against a checkout pinned to `VENDOR.md`'s `upstream_sha`, or add a Mode-V writer-specific check that stores/verifies a separate upstream-body hash after removing exactly the allowed additive skill line.

findings.title: Manifest coverage accepts class-agnostic broad globs that can unprotect adopted files
findings.why: The coverage predicate treats any row ending in `/**` as covering any matching path, regardless of row class or allowed path shape. Because NATIVE/BUILD-NEW rows are allowed to have no hashes, a manifest change can replace exact adopted rows with a broad glob such as `agents/**` or `skills/<adopted>/**` and still satisfy Rule F in Mode V, while Rule A no longer hashes those adopted files. Rule D only protects the quartet, so other adopted agents and adopted skill resources can lose hash protection.
findings.recommendation: Validate glob rows at parse time: allow globs only for NATIVE/BUILD-NEW skill roots of the exact form `skills/<name>/**`, forbid `agents/**`, and make coverage class-aware so adopted files/resources require exact adopted hash rows rather than being satisfiable by unrelated globs.

findings.title: Hashing is text-normalized, not byte-accurate
findings.why: The boundary contract claims byte-level vendoring integrity, but the verifier reads files in text mode and hashes UTF-8 re-encoding. Text mode can normalize line endings before hashing, so CRLF/LF byte drift is not represented as a byte hash difference. The same text pipeline is also used by prefix rewrite and writer body comparisons, so the implementation does not actually prove byte equality.
findings.recommendation: Use `read_bytes()` and hash raw bytes for manifest hashes. For prefix rewriting, perform a byte-level replacement on UTF-8 literals or explicitly open with `newline=''` and document that the contract is text-normalized rather than byte-identical.

findings.title: Additive-only frontmatter diff collapses duplicate lines
findings.why: Using sets removes multiplicity, so deleting one copy of a duplicated frontmatter line is invisible if another identical copy remains. The comment explicitly calls out writer.md's preserved duplicate skill line, but this implementation would not detect removal of one duplicate under Mode U. That weakens the frontmatter-additive guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Compare frontmatter as an ordered list or a `Counter` multiset after any intended prefix normalization. If order should be ignored, preserve multiplicity with `Counter`; then separately validate that every added line is exactly an allowed `skills:` entry.

findings.title: CI does not run the boundary checker's regression test suite
findings.evidence:
- name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7

      - name: Boundary contract (verify)
        working-directory: laf-adaptation
        run: uv run python scripts/check_boundary.py
findings.why: The workflow only runs the checker against the current tree. The repository also contains `laf-adaptation/scripts/test_check_boundary.py`, a stdlib unittest suite for parser hardening, Mode U pinning, prefix rewrite, resource coverage, and known residuals, but this workflow never executes it. A regression in unexercised checker logic can merge as long as the current fixture happens to pass.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI step under `working-directory: laf-adaptation` that runs `uv run python scripts/test_check_boundary.py`. If keeping exactly one shipped script is a hard architecture rule, move tests outside `laf-adaptation/scripts/` and run them from the workflow.

findings.title: Concept mapping tier keys drift between `tier_5` and `tier_4_5` shapes
findings.evidence:
concepts:
  the_grey_city:
    tier_1: "The Grey City (the city that held)"
    tier_2: "The Grey City (a city under threat that held)"
    tier_3: "The Grey City (a city under siege that held)"
    tier_5: "The Grey City"
findings.why: The Tolkien work mapping uses `tier_5`, while the universal mappings and work-mapping template use a combined upper-tier key (`tier_4_5`). Without an explicit tolerant lookup contract or validation schema, consumers resolving active tier 4/5 can miss work-specific overrides or apply universal mappings inconsistently.
findings.recommendation: Standardize the mapping key convention across templates and examples, or document and test a tolerant lookup order such as `tier_<N>` then `tier_4_5` for upper tiers.

architectural_observations.observation: CI and the opt-in pre-commit hook both run the same Mode-V command without `--upstream`; this is consistent, but it means the upstream-anchored Mode-U guarantee is not part of either automated local or PR enforcement.

The tier YAML files intentionally preserve schema drift for transformation rule names: T1-T3 use `conflict_to_cooperation` / `death_euphemism`, while T5 uses `conflict_handling` / `death_handling`. This must remain a reader-side tolerant lookup requirement.
The prose analyzer is a local CLI helper with no subprocess, eval, shell, YAML loading, or hard-coded secrets observed in the reviewed file.

uncertain: Could not verify the executable file mode for `laf-adaptation/.githooks/pre-commit` with the retrieval-only tools used for this review.
Could not validate the repository's GitHub branch-protection or mandatory-review policy that the workflow comments rely on as the backstop for Mode-V two-field manifest forgeries.
